topics.topic: Condition under which overall progress is unavailable
questions: Does unavailability mean that the project has no positive planned work at all, or that no section simultaneously has positive planned work and a recorded progress value?

Must the invariant require overall progress to be unavailable whenever no section has both positive planned work and recorded progress, even when positive planned work exists in sections that have no progress record?

quotes:
- Overall progress: `Σ(work_planned × percent) / Σ(work_planned)` over
  sections of the active version with `work_planned > 0` and a recorded
  progress (a section without a progress record is left out of both sums);
  undefined (shown unavailable) when the denominator is 0.

- INV-041: a check at `calculate_completed_work` and `calculate_overall_progress` with fixed sections: for work_planned 100.00 at 33 % and 200.00 at 50 % the completed work values are 33.00 and 100.00 and their sum 133.00; a value that rounds at the half (work_planned 0.10 at 5 % gives 0.005) is 0.01; overall progress is (100.00 × 33 + 200.00 × 50) / 300.00 = 44.33… as the formula gives it; a section without a progress record is left out of both sums and has completed work value `None`; a section with work_planned 0 is left out of overall progress; and when no section has work_planned above 0 with a recorded progress, overall progress is `None` (shown unavailable), never 0.
judgement.why: Both the formula and the required test make unavailability depend on the eligible denominator, so positive planned work without recorded progress still yields None.

questions: Is an overspent section a permitted state that produces a negative remaining balance, or a violating input that must be refused without change?

quotes: - INV-044: remaining materials show overspend as negative values, never clamped or hidden; missing data is presented explicitly, never replaced by zero unless zero is confirmed: a section without a progress record reads completion_percent None and completed_work_value None

- INV-044: the budget derivation check:
  `calculate_material_balance` and the budget view show an overspent section
  as a negative remaining, a section without a progress record reads
  completion `None` and completed work value `None`, and a project without a
  budget reads its views as not configured
  [witness: verification:budget_derivation_client_portal].
judgement.why: The invariant and its budget derivation check expressly require overspending to remain a permitted negative result rather than be refused or clamped.

topics.topic: Whether zero or negative planned amounts are accepted and how they are rejected
questions: Are zero and negative material_planned and work_planned values accepted after normalization, or refused; if refused, with what exact condition and rejection?

quotes:
A currency code, a `Decimal` amount and whether the amount must be strictly
positive (default: non-negative).

The amount quantized to two digits, ROUND_HALF_UP. An amount with more
fraction digits is rounded, never refused, and the sign rule is applied to
the rounded amount.

A9 (both amounts validated before the transaction), A18 (stable
`PortalSection` identity; imported plans never change; a missing manual
version is created as `ensure_manual_budget` does), R0-24 (active project
only), A13 (`budget.section_plan_edit`, and `budget.manual_version_create`
when created). An existing plan of the section keeps its `plan_id`.

`FinancialValidationError` for an amount; `BudgetValidationError` for an
inactive project or a `section_id` not in this project, with nothing written.
judgement.why: The operation validates both amounts with the default non-negative money rule, so zero is accepted after quantization, a negative rounded amount raises FinancialValidationError, and nothing is written.
